newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil slips slightly in lifeless market.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil slips slightly in lifeless market.

text.p: NWE fuel oil prices slipped on Tuesday in a lifeless market with players more interested in their Easter break, traders said.
High sulphur cargo prices drifted down to $81-$83 with buyers content to sit back and wait for further falls.
"End-users are fairly relaxed and will wait for numbers below $80 before they'll trade," said one buyer.
No boost was expected from the Portugese state electricity 25,000 tonne high sulphur buy tender due to be finalised on Wednesday.
"It's very quiet ahead of Easter," said one trader. "People already seem to be on holiday."

Barge prices also slipped a little, with $85.50 traded late on Monday and early on Tuesday and $85 fob ARA done later. But business was poor with major refiners chasing hard to grab bunker trade, which was at healthy levels.
Low sulphur barges were heard offered around $97 and $98 fob on Monday, with very little interest in the product.
Low sulphur cargoes were heard being indicated available into the Mediterranean but not finding buyers. Prices were being talked off slightly at $94-$96 fob.
